stories.title: Former Afghan army member arrested for alleged terrorist activities in Pakistan
summary: PESHAWAR: Security forces and law enforcement agencies have arrested a man formerly associated with the Afghan National Army (ANA) for allegedly carrying out terrorist activities in Pakistan, it emerged on Wednesday.

For their part, the Afghan Taliban have avoided taking a categorical position on the TTP and other groups, while rejecting Islamabad’s allegations that Afghanistan is being used as a base for attacks against Pakistan.
It was also reported that the Afghan Taliban engaged in unprovoked firing the night before near Kurram as security forces foiled an attempt by terrorists to cross into Pakistan.

stories.title: PM Shehbaz joins world leaders at COP31, will outline Pakistan’s climate priorities
summary: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Wednesday arrived at the COP31 Antalya Leaders’ Summit in Turkiye, where he is set to highlight Pakistan’s climate priorities, along with other world leaders.

On the sidelines of the summit, the prime minister is scheduled to hold bilateral meetings with Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan and other world leaders attending COP31 to discuss matters of mutual interest and explore avenues for strengthening bilateral cooperation.

Under UN climate agreements, developed countries, which are historically responsible for most greenhouse gas emissions, have provided financial support to help developing nations adapt to climate impacts and transition to cleaner energy.

stories.title: Asian Development Bank approves $500m loan to help Pakistan strengthen disaster preparedness
summary: ISLAMABAD: The Asian Development Bank (ADB) on Wednesday approved contingent disaster financing (CDF) facilities up to $500 million for Pakistan to withstand disasters and facilitate disaster response.

The findings came in the wake of devastating 2025 floods, which submerged entire districts, displaced millions, and wiped out livelihoods, exposing critical gaps in preparedness despite years of policy frameworks, institutional reforms, and international commitments.
The report argued that reliance on reactive disaster management has proven insufficient in the face of intensifying climate stress.

stories.title: Ex-cricketer Usman Khawaja declines to confirm if Australia's bowlers were aware of 2018 ball-tampering plot
summary: Warner, who was banned from the team for a year and cast by Cricket Australia’s investigation as the chief architect of the plot, threw his weight behind Khawaja on Monday and said his account was 100 per cent accurate.

Australian media reported Khawaja pulled out of TV and radio interviews to promote his book following the TV interview.

stories.title: De Silva, Kamindu fifties guide Sri Lanka to 221-4 in first Test against Pakistan
summary: Fifties from Dhananjaya de Silva and Kamindu Mendis helped Sri Lanka reach 221-4 at lunch on day three of the opening Test against Pakistan in Rawalpindi on Wednesday.

After resuming at 114-3, De Silva was on 87 after reaching his 21st half-century, while skipper Kusal Mendis was 21 not out, leaving the tourists still 213 runs behind Pakistan’s first innings 434-9 declared.
Mohammad Abbas and debutant Saqib Khan took early wickets before Dhananjaya de Silva and Kamindu Mendis steadied the innings with an unbeaten 49-run partnership.

stories.title: In pictures: Smog engulfs several Pakistani cities as air quality reaches ‘hazardous’ levels in Punjab
summary: Smog engulfed Pakistani skies on Wednesday as air quality continued to hover in the “hazardous” category, according to IQAir.

Of the major cities globally, IQAir ranked Lahore as the most polluted again on Wednesday, between 11am to noon, with an Air Quality Index (AQI) of 425, with levels above 300 being considered “hazardous”.
The Punjab government’s readings for the same hour showed that Muzaffargarh and Nankana Sahib’s AQI levels were at 500.

stories.title: India pollution monitors overwhelmed by toxic smog
summary: India’s air pollution monitors were overwhelmed this week by toxic smog so severe that concentrations exceeded their upper measurement limit, equivalent to 66 times the World Health Organisation’s recommended daily maximum, regulators said.

The admission comes after opposition politicians accused authorities of deliberately allowing gaps in official readings for several hours overnight Sunday into Monday, just as pollution surged with a barrage of fireworks for Diwali, the Hindu festival of lights.
Readings then hit 879 micrograms per cubic metre in the Mandir Marg locality, according to monitoring organisation IQAir, which cited data from a city government station.

stories.title: US judge rejects BBC bid to dismiss Trump defamation suit
summary: A federal judge allowed US President Donald Trump’s multi-billion dollar defamation suit against the BBC to proceed on Tuesday, rejecting a bid by the British broadcaster to dismiss the case.

Kuntz rejected the BBC’s bid to dismiss the defamation suit, but tossed the Florida protection law claim. “Whether President Trump can prove these claims and establish he sustained damages at summary judgement or trial is left for another day,” Kuntz wrote in a 40-page ruling.
The BBC documentary at issue spliced together two separate sections of Trump’s speech on January 6, 2021, making it appear that he had explicitly urged supporters to attack the US Capitol.

stories.title: Nvidia’s CEO probe and Singapore ties: Will future chip orders suffer?
summary: For instance, for the quarter that ended on July 27, 2025, over 99pc of Nvidia’s revenue billed to Singapore from selling export-controlled data centre products, including AI chips, was for orders from US-based customers.

In October 2025, it was reported that the US was investigating whether Singapore’s Megaspeed was involved in helping Chinese tech firms sidestep US export controls to obtain restricted Nvidia AI chips.
Megaspeed is under probe in Singapore and the US over possible breaches of export laws involving advanced Nvidia AI chips.

stories.title: Fight or flight? Trump mixes signals after midterms
summary: President Donald Trump’s political mantra is “fight, fight, fight.” But he has given decidedly mixed messages about whether he will do so after Republicans were hammered in the midterms.
And when Trump announced on Friday that ultraloyalist Stephen Miller would replace Susie Wiles as his chief of staff, it seemed that the gloves were finally off.

It’s a fight Trump appears to be joining with relish — saying that Hegseth “gets an ‘A’ PLUS, PLUS, PLUS” shortly after the Pentagon chief gave a press conference calling the charges a “farce.” But Hegseth will know that Trump is rarely shy of shaking up his staff.

stories.title: Fire destroys hotel’s hall during Diwali celebration in Sukkur
summary: SUKKUR: A wedding hall was destroyed when firecrackers caused a big fire inside during a function held to celebrate Diwali on Monday night.
Management of the hotel, located near the City Point Bypass, confirmed to local reporters that the blaze was caused by the fireworks set off during the celebration.
According to the hotel staff, people started rushing to safety as soon as the fire intensified.

stories.title: Jirga in Mirpur Bhutto ends 14-year-old hostility involving five communities
summary: After prolonged consultations, the Jirga pronounced its ruling, according to which a fine of Rs9.5 million was imposed on the side comprising the Bhutto, Kuriya and Narejo communities.

Chandio-Magsi feud Another Jirga, held in Qambar town, settled an old dispute between the Chandio and Magsi communities by imposing heavy fines on both the sides and ordering them to stop further bloodshed.
Both sides accepted the ruling and part of the fine amount, Rs500,000, was deposited with the Jirga on behalf of the Magsi side.

stories.title: Two killed in firing over TikTok video dispute in Charsadda
summary: CHARSADDA: Two people, including a passer-by, were killed in an exchange of fire between two rival groups over a dispute involving a TikTok video in the Majoki area within the jurisdiction of Parang police station on Tuesday.
Police said Adnan, son of Tariq and a resident of Parang Majoki, and passer-by Asghar Ali were killed in the firing.

Meanwhile, Saleem Jan, brother of the deceased passer-by Asghar Ali, told police that his brother was caught in the crossfire between two rival groups, identified as Waqar and others on one side and Hilal and others on the other, and was killed.

summary: The Pakistan Stock Exchange (PSX) continued its positive run in mid-day trading on Wednesday, with the benchmark KSE-100 Index rising 1,111.05 points, or 0.62 per cent, to 180,446.29.
Index-heavy stocks such as UBL, MCB, MEBL, NBP, OGDC, PPL and SSGC traded higher at various stages of the session.
The Index is still subject to further movement before the close of trading.

stories.title: Hammad Azhar complains of ‘CCTV surveillance in prison cell’
summary: LAHORE: PTI leader Hammad Azhar on Tuesday complained to an antiterrorism court (ATC) about inadequate facilities in jail, alleging he had been kept under constant surveillance through two CCTV cameras installed in his cell, including one monitoring even the bathroom.
The PTI leader requested the court to provide him with at least a chair and a table in his cell, so that he could continue writing. “I can manage without a bed or mattress,” he added.

summary: GUJRAT: A man was allegedly shot dead by four unidentified suspects, in alleged connivance with his son and wife, at Kulachor village in Jalalpur Jattan Saddar police precincts.

Police claimed to have arrested Hasan and Kausar and registered a case against the four unidentified attackers and the two nominated suspects, under sections 302, 109, 148 and 149 of the Pakistan Penal Code.
As per the police, a UoG student, ‘W’, alleged in his complaint that his friend ‘Y’, who runs a barber shop at the village, called him to the shop where he raped him at gunpoint.

stories.title: CDA challenges court order protecting Bari Imam House from demolition in Islamabad
summary: The CDA sealed Bari Imam House on Oct 30 in a joint operation with the district administration, claiming the structure stands on government land and was among properties identified in its anti-encroachment drive.
The CDA further states that the shrine land is recorded on entirely different Khasra numbers – 277, 665, 677, 678, 679 and 680 – in the name of Darbar Aalia Hazrat Bari Abdul Latif Shah.

The premises described by the petitioner neither form part of the shrine nor fall within the Darbar’s land, the authority maintains, adding that the subject land vests in the CDA and the petitioner has no lawful right, title or interest in it.

stories.title: Islamabad ATC refuses to drop terror charges in PAF officer murder case
summary: ISLAMABAD: An Anti-Terrorism Court (ATC) on Tuesday rejected a defence plea seeking the removal of terrorism-related charges from the murder case of late Group Captain Asim Tariq, ruling that the trial would continue before the anti-terrorism court.

During the proceedings, the defence counsel argued that the provisions of the Anti-Terrorism Act were not applicable to the case and requested the court to decide the matter before recording statements of prosecution witnesses.
The prosecutor further argued that if the court found at any stage of the trial that the terrorism provisions were not applicable, it had the authority to transfer the case to the appropriate forum.

stories.title: Two killed in Ukrainian drone attack on Russia's Smolensk, Leningrad hit by year's largest attack
summary: Two people were killed in a massive Ukrainian drone attack on Russia’s Smolensk region overnight, Governor Vasily Anokhin said on Wednesday. “Overnight, the Smolensk region came under a massive drone attack by the Ukrainian armed forces.
Air defence forces of the Defence Ministry destroyed 37 enemy drones. … Two people were killed,” Anokhin said on the Russian social media platform Max.

Meanwhile, the drone attack repelled in the Leningrad region overnight on November 11 was the largest since the start of 2026, according to calculations by Russia’s TASS news agency based on data from Governor Alexander Drozdenko.

stories.title: Karachi likely to receive light rain, drizzle on Friday: PMD
summary: Light rain and drizzle are expected at isolated places in Karachi on Friday, while most parts of Sindh are likely to experience dry and cool weather, the Pakistan Meteorological Department (PMD) said on Wednesday.
The department said dry weather with cool nights was likely to prevail across most parts of Sindh, while misty mornings were expected in the province's plains.

stories.title: Ngumoha targets Ballon d'Or after Kane inspiration
summary: Liverpool winger Rio Ngumoha said Harry Kane's Ballon d'Or victory can inspire a new generation of English footballers, including himself, to follow in ‌the Bayern Munich striker's footsteps and be recognised as the world's best.

summary: Mumbai Indians have traded captain Hardik Pandya to Punjab Kings ‌in exchange for left-arm seamer Arshdeep Singh ahead of ‌next year's Indian ⁠Premier League (IPL), ​organisers of ​the Twenty20 ‌competition said on Wednesday.
All-rounder ​Pandya has been Mumbai captain since 2024.
Arshdeep, who spent eight seasons with Punjab, will join Jasprit Bumrah in a formidable pace attack at Mumbai.

summary: New ​Zealand ​have included Devon Conway, Rachin Ravindra and Tom Blundell in a strong squad for the test series against India with all three aiming ‌to be fit for the first test next week, New Zealand Cricket said on Wednesday.

stories.title: PM Shehbaz to address COP31 summit in Turkiye, highlight climate justice
summary: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif is scheduled to address the high-level segment of the United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31) in Antalya, Turkiye, on Wednesday, highlighting Pakistan's position on climate justice and the concerns of countries affected by climate change.

A day earlier, the prime minister arrived in Turkiye to attend the World Leaders' Summit being held as part of the 31st Conference of the Parties (COP31) to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC).

According to the statement, the prime minister would also deliver Pakistan's national statement at the COP31 summit, highlighting climate justice and the concerns of countries affected by climate change at the international level.

stories.title: Afghan national arrested in Tirah Valley for plotting terrorist attacks in Pakistan: K-P police
summary: Today, we have achieved success with the arrest of an Afghan terrorist who was planning attacks in Pakistan,” Babar said.

He said the arrested suspect was not an isolated case and that such networks continued to operate. “These people take advantage of the cover of darkness and enter Pakistan to carry out attacks, but they do not realise that the sons of Pakistan are waiting for them,” he added.
He added that anyone attempting to enter Pakistan to carry out attacks would find their way blocked, as security forces, society and the government stood united against them.

stories.title: Fazlur Rehman’s son skips NAB summons
summary: Mr Mehmood had been directed to appear before the investigation team at 11am on Nov 10 to explain his position on alleged irregularities in 4,252 appointments made at Pakistan Post during his tenure as federal minister in 2022-23.
According to the notice, the Establishment Division had authorised recruitment against 3,938 posts at Pakistan Post, but 4,252 people were allegedly appointed, exceeding the approved strength.
The bureau is also examining allegations that permanent appointments were made despite a recommendation for contractual recruitment, placing an additional financial burden on Pakistan Post.

stories.title: Khawaja rejects 'witch hunt' claims over Sandpapergate
summary: Former Australia opening batsman Usman Khawaja denied trying to spark a "witch hunt" over Sandpapergate, as calls grow to reopen a probe into the ball-tampering scandal.
Khawaja said in his autobiography released on Tuesday that the 2018 plot had been common knowledge throughout the team and not limited to a small number of players.
A Cricket Australia investigation found they were the only three players with prior knowledge of the plot.

stories.title: SC disposes of Imaan Mazari, Hadi Chattha's trial appeals as infructuous
summary: The Supreme Court (SC) on Wednesday disposed of appeals challenging the trial in the barriers removal case involving Human rights lawyers Imaan Mazari and Hadi Ali Chattha, declaring the matter infructuous as the trial had already been completed.

On Friday, Imaan and Hadi filed appeals against their convictions in the case in the Islamabad High Court (IHC), along with separate applications seeking suspension of their sentences and release on bail pending the outcome of the appeals.

Advocate Faisal Siddiqui informed the bench that the anti-terrorism court (ATC) had completed the entire trial in jail within 22 days. “The trial has already been completed, and the case has now become infructuous,” Justice Mazhar observed.

stories.title: Rain, snow in northern parts of the country from today
summary: In Punjab and Islamabad, light rain, wind and thunderstorms are expected in the capital city, the Potohar region, Mianwali, Khushab, Bhakkar, Sargodha, Murree and adjoining areas on Wednesday (today).
Rain, wind and thunderstorms are also expected in Dera Ghazi Khan, Layyah, Bhakkar and Multan on Nov 12.

However, isolated rain, wind and thunderstorms, accompanied by hailstorms, are expected in Duki, Harnai, Pishin, Sherani, Surab, Zhob, Barkhan, Musakhel, Quetta, Ziarat, Chaman, Qila Abdullah, Qila Saifullah, Kalat and Khuzdar on the night of Nov 11 and Nov 12.

stories.title: Public Accounts Committee seeks to delay power firms’ sell-off until asset valuation
summary: The proposal came after Auditor General of Paki­stan Maqbool Ahmad Gon­dal raised concerns that the government was relying on outdated valuations of public assets during a meeting of the PAC to examine the audit reports of the Power Division and its attached entities for 2024-25.
She called for another meeting in three weeks to review the privatisation process and ensure that the assets were assigned their correct market values before further steps were taken.
The Privatisation Commission and the Power Division were directed to submit detailed reports at the next meeting.

stories.title: Peshawar ATC reissues arrest warrants for Sohail Afridi in Radio Pakistan attack case
summary: An anti-terrorism court (ATC) in Peshawar on Wednesday reissued arrest warrants for Sohail Afridi, the suspended Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P) Chief Minister in the May 9 attack case, while extending the interim bail of three former provincial ministers until November 17.
The case relates to the attack on and arson at the Radio Pakistan building in Peshawar during violent protests on May 9 and 10, 2023, following the arrest of PTI founder Imran Khan.
It was registered on the complaint of Radio Pakistan, which nominated Afridi, former ministers Taimur Saleem Jhagra, Kamran Bangash and Irfan Saleem, and Aamir Khan Chamkani.
